context.note: Identifies a human account, as distinct from an agent account; pairs with the Agent badge. English reads "Human" (not "Person") so the pair contrasts human with AI. Use the concise noun for a human being, not a job title or a generic word for an individual.

fr.verdict: PASS. 'Humain' (substantive) is the standard French term opposed to IA/agent ('humain ou IA'); unambiguous, unlike the previous 'Personne' (also 'nobody', and 'individual' not human-vs-AI). One word, neutral register, masculine generic acceptable for a neutral badge; pairs cleanly with 'Agent'.

es.verdict: PASS. 'Humano' is the natural one-word noun for the human side of 'humano o IA'; the previous 'Persona' named an individual. Neutral register, masculine generic acceptable for a badge; pairs with 'Agente'.

zh-CN.verdict: PASS. '人类' is the established label for the human role opposite an AI/智能体 in Chinese AI products (e.g. role labels 人类/AI); '个人' meant 'personal/individual' and read as an account type. '真人' would add a 'real person / live-action' nuance; '人' alone is too bare for a badge. Two characters, terse per the style guide, balances '智能体'.

ru.verdict: PASS (unchanged bytes, re-bound to the new English source). 'Человек' is exactly the noun for a human being and the usual opposite of ИИ/агент ('человек или ИИ'); no clearer single-word alternative exists ('Персона' is the individual/persona sense, 'Люди' is plural). Pairs with 'Агент'.

vi.verdict: PASS (unchanged bytes, re-bound to the new English source). 'Con người' is the species-sense noun for a human being, the standard contrast with AI ('con người và AI'); 'Người' alone is generic (person/someone) and 'Cá nhân' is 'individual'. Pairs with 'Tác nhân'.

ur.verdict: PASS. 'انسان' is the everyday Urdu noun for a human being and the natural contrast with AI/مصنوعی ذہانت; the previous 'شخص' meant individual/person. Native, not over-Persianised, matches the style guide's everyday educated register; single RTL word, no bidi controls, beside 'ایجنٹ'.

hi.verdict: PASS. 'मानव' is the standard Hindi noun for 'human' in human-vs-AI usage ('मानव बनाम एआई'); the previous 'व्यक्ति' meant individual. Common rather than heavily Sanskritised ('मनुष्य' would be more formal; 'इंसान' more colloquial), so it fits the style guide's everyday standard Hindi; pairs with 'एजेंट'.

observations.note: Masculine generic (Humain/Humano) on a badge that may label a woman. Accepted: neutral one-word labels conventionally take the masculine generic, and neither style guide asks for inclusive forms; no shorter neutral alternative exists.
'人类' is species-level ('humankind') but is the established role label opposite AI in Chinese AI products; kept over '真人' (live/real-person nuance).
No rendered frame inspected. Every value is shorter than or equal to the agent badge in cells except fr/es/ru/vi, all <= 9 cells for a one-word badge; no fit claim is made.
